questions.question: The famous musician, Appa Jalgaonkar is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harmonium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Appa Jalgaonkar** played the **harmonium.**
 
• He was well-known as accompanist of **singer Bhimsen Joshi.**
 
• **Amir Khan, Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, and Hirabai Barodekar** were some of the **singers** with whom Appa Jalgaonkar collaborated.
 
• He was given the **prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award **for his accomplishments in harmonium playing.
 
• On **September 16th,** he passed away in **Pune at the age of 87.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmonium:**

 
 
• It is a **free-reed keyboard** instrument.
 
• It emits sound when air is forced through **metal reeds screwed over slots** in metal frames with close tolerance by** foot-operated bellows** through a **pressure-equalizing air reservoir.**
 
 
 
• **Tabla:**
 
 
• It is the most widely used instrument for **dance, vocal, and instrumental music.**
 
 
 
• **Sarod**:
 
 
• It is a stringed musical instrument of the lute family that is common to the **Hindustani music.**
 
 
 
• **Violin:**
 
 
• It is a **wooden chordophone,** a **type of string instrument.**

questions.question: Begum Akhtar a famous singer from India is known for which of the following genres?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal music**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghazal is a poetic** form that originated in **Arabic literature** and was adapted into **South Asian music**, primarily in **Urdu and Persian.**
 
• **Themes: **The lyrics often explore themes of love, loss, and longing, with a strong **focus on emotional expression **and lyrical beauty.
 
• **Musical Structure:** Typically performed with a combination of vocals and instruments like the** harmonium, tabla, and sitar**.
 
• The music is characterized by its **melodious and soulful tunes.**
 
• Ghazals are usually performed with intricate improvisations and ornamentations, showcasing the singer’s vocal skills and emotional depth.
 
• **Prominent Artists**: Notable ghazal singers include **Jagjit Singh**, **Ghulam Ali, and Mehdi Hassan**, who have popularized the genre and brought it to a global audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sufi Music:**

 
 
• **Sufi music** is deeply rooted in** Islamic mysticism** and aims to foster a spiritual connection with the divine.
 
• Commonly features instruments like the** tabla, harmonium,** and flute, enhancing the meditative and devotional atmosphere.
 
• **Themes:** Focuses on themes of divine love, longing, and the pursuit of spiritual enlightenment.
 
• **Notable Artists:** Prominent artists include** Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, Abida Parveen, and Rahat Fateh Ali Khan,** who have popularized Sufi music globally.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic music:**
 
 
• Carnatic music is a **classical music tradition from South India,** distinct from Hindustani music of North India.
 
• Features complex compositions in various forms such as **Kriti, Varnam, and Padams, **focusing on melodic and rhythmic precision.
 
• Emphasizes the use of ragas (melodic scales) and talas (rhythmic cycles) to create intricate and expressive performances.
 
• Commonly uses instruments like the **veena, mridangam, and violin, **often accompanied by vocal performances.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__****Indian Classical Music:**

 
• **Hindustani Music (North India)**:

 
 
• Forms: Includes dhrupad, khayal, thumri.
 
• Instruments: **Sitar, tabla, harmonium.**
 
• **Notable Artists: Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain.**
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music (South India):**
 
 
• Forms: Includes kriti, varnam, padams.
 
• Instruments: **Veena, mridangam, violin.**
 
• **Notable Artists: M. S. Subbulakshmi, Lalgudi Jayaraman.**

questions.question: Tansen, the music legend was a courtier in which of the following courts before coming to Akbar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rewa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tansen** began his illustrious career as a **court musician** in the court of **Raja Ramchandra Singh of Rewa,** also known as **Raja Ramchandra**.
 
• He served as both the court poet and vocalist for Raja Ramchandra Singh before catching the attention of **Emperor Akbar**.
 
• Renowned for his mastery of the **Dhrupad style of singing**, Tansen was not only a vocalist but also an instrumentalist who composed numerous ragas.
 
• During his tenure in the court of Raja Ramchandra Singh, Tansen's musical talents gained widespread acclaim.
 
• Emperor Akbar, upon hearing of Tansen's prodigious abilities, requested his presence at his court through a 'firman' sent to the king.
 
• Tansen was appointed as one of the Navaratnas (Nine Jewels) in Akbar's court, where he was bestowed with the titles of 'Mian' and Kanthabharan Vanivilas.
 
• Tansen quickly became a favorite of Emperor Akbar after joining his court in **1556**.
 
• Legend has it that Tansen's rendition of Raag Deepak was so powerful that it could light even extinguished candles, showcasing the extraordinary depth of his musical talent and influence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abu'l-Fath Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar,** popularly known as **Akbar the Great, **or Akbar I, was the **third Mughal emperor**, reigning from **1556 to 1605.**
 
• Following the reign of his father, Humayun, Akbar ascended to the throne under the **regency of Bairam Khan, **who played a pivotal role in expanding and consolidating Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During Akbar's rule, Mughal India experienced significant economic growth and stability. The empire's economy tripled in size and wealth, fostering commercial expansion and promoting the flourishing of an Indo-Persian culture.
 
• Akbar's reign is characterized by his efforts to create a strong and prosperous empire, marked by administrative reforms, religious tolerance, and cultural patronage.
 
• After his death in 1605, Akbar was succeeded as emperor by his son, Prince Salim, who later became known as Jahangir.

questions.question: Pandit Ravi Shankar, founder of National Orchestra of India, was a __________ player.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar** was a legendary sitar player and composer.
 
• He was instrumental in popularizing Indian classical music in the Western world.
 
• In addition to founding the National Orchestra of India, he collaborated with many international artists, including George Harrison of The Beatles.
 
• His contributions to music have earned him numerous awards, including Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar** was born on April 7, 1920, and passed away on December 11, 2012.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan** in 1981 and the **Padma Bhushan** in 1967.
 
• Shankar's influence extended beyond music; he played a significant role in cultural exchange between India and the world.
 
• He also served as a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Indian Parliament, from 1986 to 1992.
 
• His autobiography, "Raga Mala," provides a deep insight into his life and musical journey.

questions.question: The famous musician Satyadev Pawar is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Violin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Satya Dev Pawar began his study of music at the age of eleven in the quondam Jodhpur State of Rajasthan, **India.
 
• Late His Highness Maharaja Hanumant Singhji patronized youthful **Pawar to train on the violin under Ustad Ali Akbar Khan( the notorious son of Baba Allauddin Khan) therefore continuing the unbroken musical lineage," the Seni Baba Allaudin Gharana," descended from Mian Tansen,** the principal musician in the Moghul Emperor Akbar's court in 15th century India.
 
• latterly, Satyadev Pawar apprenticed under Pandit Ravi Shankar, another outstanding Baba convert, gained fame as one of the best-known shishyas of these great Gurus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecadfa2aebbde6f5d8518a1b79e60590ca022b7aa48797ddac8c90a13d89ae3a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shehnai:**

 
 
• Shehnai is a wind instrument made of **wood **and** metal**.
 
• Used in religious observances, this instrument is set up in the colorful corridor of North India.
 
• It's considered to be an auspicious instrument and is played in social observances.
 
• Also a Northern Indian musical instrument.
 
• Some important shehnai players are** Anant Lal**, **Bismillah Khan**, **S. Ballesh**, **Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan**, and **Raghunath Prasanna**.
 
 
 
• **Veena:**
 
 
• Firstly created in the** south of India**, the veena is a plucked string instrument.
 
• This actually belongs to the family of **chordophone instruments **of India.
 
• The veena in numerous corridors of the country has different types which are **Rudra Veena**, **Sarasvati Veena**, and **Vichitra Veena**.
 
• **Carnatic music**, in the south of India, extensively uses the veena.
 
 
 
• **Sitar:**
 
 
• Sitar is a generally used stringed instrument in South Asian countries similar to **Bangladesh**, **India**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The Sitar instrument is a plucked stringed instrument that contains portable frets and a gourd resonator.
 
• “ Sitar ” is deduced from the Persian word “ Sehtar ”( seh navigator) meaning “**three-stringed**”.

questions.question: Famous musician Talvin Singh is associated with playing the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tabla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Talvin Singh **is an English musician, producer, and composer known for his expertise in playing the tabla.
 
• He gained recognition for pioneering a unique fusion of Indian classical music with drum and bass, contributing to the emergence of the electronica subgenre known as Asian Underground.
 
• Singh's collaborations with artists like Siouxsie and the Banshees and Björk in the early 1990s propelled him into the spotlight.
 
• His debut album, "Ok," released in 1999, earned him the prestigious Mercury Music Prize.
 
• In 2010, Singh received an award at the UK Asian Music Awards for his "Commitment to Scene." In recognition of his contributions to music, he was honored with an OBE in the 2014 Birthday Honours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A tabla** is a pair of hand drums originating from the Indian subcontinent. Since the 18th century, it has held a central role as the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is versatile, being played solo, accompanying other instruments and vocals, and as part of larger ensembles.
 
• The tabla is prevalent in popular and folk music performances across India, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
 
• It holds significance in the devotional practices of Hinduism and Sikhism, often used during bhajan and kirtan singing.
 
• Sufi musicians commonly use the tabla in qawwali performances, and it is a prominent feature in dance forms like Kathak. As a rhythmic instrument, the tabla plays a crucial role in various musical traditions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uday Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uday Shankar, **an Indian dancer and choreographer, gained renown for melding **European theatrical techniques **with Indian classical, folk, and tribal dance forms.
 
• He introduced this innovative style, which he initially termed** "Hi-dance,"** garnering attention in India, Europe, and the United States during the 1920s.
 
• Beginning his formal artistic education in **Mumbai in 1917,** Shankar was exposed to a diverse array of dance forms, including Indian classical, folk, and ballet, during his time in Europe.
 
• He coined the term "Hi-dance" to describe his fusion style, later evolving it into "Modern Dance."
 
• In 1965, he established the Uday Shankar Centre for Dance in Kolkata, contributing to the promotion and preservation of dance heritage.
 
• Shankar's contributions to the field of dance were recognized with prestigious accolades, including the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship** in 1962 and the** Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian honor, bestowed upon him in 1971.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Guru Bipin Singha** is recognized as the pioneer of Manipuri Dance.
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was an Indian dancer, composer, singer, and exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance in India.
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a legendary Indian classical dancer, guru, and exponent of Odissi dance, credited with the revival and popularization of this classical dance form in the 20th century.

questions.question: Hari Prasad Chaurasia, an Indian flutist, is associated with which of the following music gharanas?
